environment.description: Same Node.js 18 Apollo GraphQL server packaged as a container image deployed via AWS Lambda with a Function URL. The Function URL is configured with AuthType: AWS_IAM. The Lambda execution role has a resource-based policy that only grants lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl to principals within the same AWS Organization (condition: aws:PrincipalOrgID). The Lambda runs in a VPC with no NAT gateway (egress restricted). The /tmp filesystem in Lambda is an ephemeral 512MB mount that is isolated per invocation instance and starts empty - no external process can pre-create symlinks in the Lambda's /tmp. Additionally, the function's resource policy does not include any AllowPublicAccess statement, and the OrgID condition uses StringEquals (not StringLike) preventing wildcard bypass.

config.network: Lambda Function URL with AuthType AWS_IAM, VPC-attached with no NAT/IGW
config.auth: Function URL IAM auth - unsigned requests receive 403 Forbidden before reaching handler
config.resource_policy: lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl granted only to aws:PrincipalOrgID eq o-abc123def4
config.filesystem: /tmp is ephemeral per Lambda execution environment, 512MB, no shared mount
config.symlink_protection: No external process can write to Lambda /tmp; each cold start begins with empty /tmp
config.iam_signing: Requests must include valid SigV4 signature from an IAM principal within the Organization
